page.title: Community Manager vs Community Agency Comparison
page.description: Compare in-house community manager costs and responsibilities against outsourced community agency services including moderation, programming, and reporting.
page.h1: Should you hire a community manager or a community agency?
page.definition: Community management is the practice of building and nurturing an audience around a brand through platforms like Discord, Slack, or Circle, involving strategy, moderation, programming, and member support. It includes setting brand voice, onboarding new members, running events, and reporting on engagement metrics.
page.quick_answer: Start by defining which tasks you keep in-house — strategy and brand voice — and which you outsource — moderation, onboarding, and reporting — then request a scope-based quote from a community-as-a-service provider.

sections.h2: What does an in-house community manager cost?

blocks.p: An in-house community manager costs more than salary alone when you add benefits, tools, training, and overhead.

ul: Base salary plus employer taxes and benefits
Community platform licences such as Discord or Slack premium tiers
Management time for hiring, onboarding, and performance reviews

sections.h2: What does a community agency deliver?

blocks.p: A community agency provides a bundle of operational services that cover day-to-day execution while you retain strategic control.

ul: Moderation across time zones and risk levels
Programming such as AMAs, events, and content series
Reporting on engagement, sentiment, and growth metrics

sections.h2: Which tasks should stay in-house and which can be outsourced?

blocks.p: Keep strategy and brand decisions internal; outsource execution-heavy work that requires coverage and scale.

sections.h2: What platforms do community teams typically use?

blocks.p: Most teams standardise on one primary platform and supplement with others for specific audiences.

ul: Discord for real-time chat and voice
Slack for professional or B2B communities
Circle for course-based or membership communities
Khoros or Higher Logic for enterprise-scale communities

sections.h2: How is community as a service scoped and priced?

blocks.p: Community as a service is quoted by scope covering coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk, and programming complexity; West Peek Productions scopes each engagement and does not publish a fixed price list.

faq.q: Can a single community manager handle both strategy and daily moderation?
faq.a: A single manager can cover both early on, but as member volume grows the split between strategic planning and real-time moderation becomes unsustainable without burnout or quality loss. Consider adding a part-time moderator or agency support once daily active users exceed a threshold that strains one person.

faq.q: What coverage hours do agencies typically offer?
faq.a: Agencies often provide tiered coverage from business hours only to twenty-four-seven moderation, with pricing scaled to the number of shifts and response-time commitments. Typical tiers include eight-hour, sixteen-hour, and full-day coverage with defined service-level agreements for response times.

faq.q: How do you measure community return on investment?
faq.a: Track owned audience growth such as email subscribers and active members, conversion rates from community to product sign-ups, and retention lift compared to non-community customers. Combine these with qualitative sentiment analysis and referral traffic to build a full picture of community value.

faq.q: Does West Peek Productions manage communities directly?
faq.a: West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid, and webinar events and sets up marketing, content, and creative operations; community management is scoped separately as a service engagement. The team quotes community-as-a-service by coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk, and programming complexity without a fixed price list.
